entities.name: Swatch Group
entities.description: World's largest watch group by volume, formed in 1983 from the SSIH/ASUAG merger; owns Omega, Breguet, Longines, Tissot, ETA and more.

entities.name: Richemont
entities.description: Geneva-based luxury conglomerate whose Specialist Watchmakers include Cartier, Vacheron Constantin, Jaeger-LeCoultre, IWC, Panerai and A. Lange & Söhne.

entities.name: LVMH
entities.description: Luxury group whose Watches division includes TAG Heuer, Zenith, Hublot, Bulgari and Louis Vuitton; also owns Tiffany & Co. and Chaumet.

entities.name: Kering
entities.description: French luxury group (formerly PPR) that owned Girard-Perregaux and Ulysse Nardin until 2022 and still runs Gucci watches.

entities.name: Hans Wilsdorf Foundation
entities.description: Private Geneva foundation created by Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf in 1945; the sole owner of Rolex.

entities.name: Seiko Group
entities.description: Japanese group descended from K. Hattori (1881), parent of Seiko, Grand Seiko, Credor and King Seiko.

entities.name: Seiko Epson
entities.description: Seiko-family electronics company (Suwa Seikosha lineage) that took control of Orient in 2009 and absorbed it in 2017.

entities.name: Citizen Watch Co.
entities.description: Tokyo-based group owning Citizen, Bulova, Frederique Constant, Alpina, Arnold & Son, Angelus and movement makers Miyota and La Joux-Perret.

entities.name: Fossil Group
entities.description: Texas fashion-watch group that owns Fossil, Skagen and Zodiac and makes licensed watches for Michael Kors, Emporio Armani and others.

entities.name: Movado Group
entities.description: New Jersey watch group owning Movado, Ebel, Concord, MVMT and Olivia Burton and holding licences such as Hugo Boss and Tommy Hilfiger.

entities.name: Timex Group
entities.description: Parent of Timex that also produces licensed watches for Guess (via Sequel) and Versace (via Vertime).

entities.name: Festina Group
entities.description: Barcelona-based group of Miguel Rodríguez owning Festina, Lotus, Jaguar, Perrelet and movement maker Soprod.

entities.name: Sowind Group
entities.description: La Chaux-de-Fonds holding of Girard-Perregaux and Ulysse Nardin, independent again since a 2022 management buyout from Kering.

entities.name: Citychamp Watch & Jewellery Group
entities.description: Hong Kong-listed group owning Eterna and a controlling stake in Ernest Borel; owned Corum from 2013 to 2025.

entities.name: Tata Group
entities.description: Indian conglomerate whose Titan Company (a joint venture with Tamil Nadu's TIDCO) is India's largest watchmaker.

entities.name: DKSH
entities.description: Swiss market-expansion services group that has held Maurice Lacroix since 2011 and briefly owned Glycine.

entities.name: Partners Group
entities.description: Swiss private-equity firm that became Breitling's majority owner in 2022.

entities.name: CVC Capital Partners
entities.description: Private-equity firm that bought Breitling from the Schneider family in 2017.

entities.name: Damiani Group
entities.description: Italian jewellery group that bought Baume & Mercier from Richemont, completing the deal in July 2026.

entities.name: SSIH
entities.description: Société Suisse pour l'Industrie Horlogère, formed in 1930 by Omega and Tissot; merged with ASUAG in 1983 to create what became the Swatch Group.

entities.name: ASUAG
entities.description: Allgemeine Schweizerische Uhrenindustrie AG, the 1931 holding of ébauche makers including ETA; merged with SSIH in 1983.

entities.name: Les Manufactures Horlogères (LMH)
entities.description: VDO/Mannesmann-controlled holding of IWC, Jaeger-LeCoultre and A. Lange & Söhne, sold to Richemont in 2000.

entities.name: TAG Group (Techniques d'Avant Garde)
entities.description: Mansour Ojjeh's investment group that bought Heuer in 1985, creating TAG Heuer, before selling it to LVMH in 1999.

entities.name: Investcorp
entities.description: Investment firm that owned Breguet and Nouvelle Lemania from the late 1980s until selling them to the Swatch Group in 1999.

entities.name: Chaumet
entities.description: Parisian jeweller (LVMH-owned since 1999) whose Chaumet brothers owned Breguet from 1970 to 1987.

entities.name: Sandoz Family Foundation
entities.description: Swiss family foundation that owns Parmigiani Fleurier and the Vaucher Manufacture Fleurier movement maker.

entities.name: MELB Holding
entities.description: Meylan-family holding that has owned H. Moser & Cie since 2012.

entities.name: VEB Glashütter Uhrenbetriebe (GUB)
entities.description: East German state combine that absorbed Glashütte's nationalised watch firms from 1951; its privatisation produced Glashütte Original.

entities.name: Nokia
entities.description: Finnish telecoms company that bought Withings in 2016 and sold it back to co-founder Éric Carreel in 2018.

entities.name: Tiffany & Co.
entities.description: New York jeweller and retailer (LVMH-owned since 2021) famous for co-signed Patek Philippe and Rolex dials.

entities.name: Bucherer
entities.description: Lucerne-based watch and jewellery retailer, the world's largest Rolex retailer, bought by Rolex in 2023.

entities.name: Watches of Switzerland Group
entities.description: UK-listed luxury watch retailer that acquired Hodinkee in 2024.

entities.name: Hodinkee
entities.description: New York watch media and commerce company (founded 2008 by Ben Clymer) known for limited-edition collaborations.

entities.name: Crown & Caliber
entities.description: Atlanta pre-owned watch e-tailer bought by Hodinkee in 2021; its digital assets went to European Watch Company in 2024.

entities.name: Ethos Watch Boutiques
entities.description: India's largest luxury watch retailer, which acquired the Favre-Leuba brand from Titan in 2023.

entities.name: ETA SA
entities.description: Swatch Group's ébauche giant (spun out of Eterna in 1932), maker of the 2824, 2892 and Valjoux 7750 families.

entities.name: Sellita
entities.description: La Chaux-de-Fonds movement maker, long an ETA assembler, whose SW200/SW300 families became the main alternative to ETA.

entities.name: Kenissi
entities.description: Tudor's movement manufacture (20% owned by Chanel), supplying Tudor, Breitling, Chanel, Norqain, Fortis and Bell & Ross.

entities.name: Vaucher Manufacture Fleurier
entities.description: High-end movement maker in Fleurier owned by the Sandoz Family Foundation and 25% by Hermès; supplies Parmigiani, Hermès, Richard Mille and Corum.

entities.name: Valjoux
entities.description: Historic Vallée de Joux chronograph specialist (Valjoux 72, 7750), absorbed into ETA in the 1980s.

entities.name: Lemania
entities.description: Vallée de Joux chronograph maker behind the Lemania 2310 used by Omega, Patek Philippe and Vacheron; became Manufacture Breguet.

entities.name: La Joux-Perret
entities.description: La Chaux-de-Fonds movement maker (formerly Jaquet SA), owned by Citizen since 2012.

entities.name: Soprod
entities.description: Swiss movement maker owned by the Festina Group since 2008, known for the M100 and P024 calibres.

entities.name: Dubois Dépraz
entities.description: Vallée de Joux complication-module specialist that co-developed the 1969 Chronomatic Calibre 11.

entities.name: Audemars Piguet Renaud & Papi
entities.description: Le Locle complications workshop founded by Dominique Renaud and Giulio Papi, majority-owned by Audemars Piguet; a training ground for many independents.

entities.name: Frédéric Piguet
entities.description: Vallée de Joux fine-movement maker acquired with Blancpain by Swatch Group in 1992 and merged into Blancpain in 2010.

entities.name: Miyota
entities.description: Citizen's movement subsidiary, whose 8215, 9015/9039 and 90S5 calibres power countless microbrands.

entities.name: Seiko Instruments (SII/TMI)
entities.description: Seiko Group movement arm whose Time Module unit sells the NH35 automatic and VK meca-quartz calibres to third parties.

entities.name: Ronda
entities.description: Swiss quartz and mechanical movement maker, the main supplier of Shinola's movements.

entities.name: Agenhor
entities.description: Jean-Marc Wiederrecht's Geneva complication house behind Van Cleef & Arpels' Poetic Complications and many Hermès modules.

entities.name: Concepto Watch Factory
entities.description: La Chaux-de-Fonds movement developer and Jacob & Co.'s main partner for complications such as the Astronomia.

entities.name: Dimier 1738
entities.description: Movement manufacture acquired by Bovet owner Pascal Raffy in 2006; makes Bovet's calibres and balance springs.

entities.name: Minerva
entities.description: Villeret chronograph manufacture founded 1858, acquired by Richemont in 2006 and run as Montblanc's Villeret workshop.

entities.name: Techniques Horlogères Appliquées (THA)
entities.description: Complications workshop founded 1989 by Vianney Halter, F.P. Journe and Denis Flageollet; bought by Bucherer in 2007.

entities.name: Aegler (Rolex Bienne)
entities.description: Bienne movement maker that supplied Rolex from its early years and was merged into Rolex in 2004.

entities.name: La Fabrique du Temps Louis Vuitton
entities.description: Geneva complications workshop founded by ex-Gérald Genta watchmakers, owned by Louis Vuitton since 2011.

entities.name: mb-microtec
entities.description: Bernese inventor of tritium gas light sources (Trigalight), owner of the Traser brand and supplier to Luminox.

entities.name: G&F Châtelain
entities.description: La Chaux-de-Fonds case and component maker bought by Chanel in 1993; the base of Chanel's watchmaking.

entities.name: Donzé Cadrans
entities.description: Le Locle enamel-dial workshop acquired by Ulysse Nardin in 2011.

entities.name: Natéber
entities.description: La Chaux-de-Fonds dial maker acquired by Hermès in 2012.

entities.name: Gérald Genta
entities.description: Designer (1931–2011) of the Royal Oak, Nautilus, Ingenieur SL, Polerouter, Pasha and Bulgari Bulgari.

entities.name: Jörg Hysek
entities.description: Designer of the Vacheron Constantin 222, Breguet Marine, TAG Heuer Kirium and Seiko Arctura.

entities.name: Eric Giroud
entities.description: Geneva designer behind many MB&F Horological Machines, Harry Winston's Opus 9 and work for Vacheron, Van Cleef & Arpels and Tissot.

entities.name: Emmanuel Gueit
entities.description: Designer of the 1993 Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Offshore; later revived Rolex's Cellini line.

entities.name: Jean-Claude Biver
entities.description: Executive who revived Blancpain, repositioned Omega, created Hublot's Big Bang and led TAG Heuer and LVMH's watch division.

entities.name: Nicolas G. Hayek
entities.description: Engineer-consultant (1928–2010) who merged SSIH and ASUAG, launched Swatch and led the Swatch Group.

entities.name: Hans Wilsdorf
entities.description: Founder of Rolex (1905, as Wilsdorf & Davis) and Tudor, and of the foundation that owns them.

entities.name: Maximilian Büsser
entities.description: Created Harry Winston's Opus series as head of its watch division (1998–2005), then founded MB&F in 2005.

entities.name: George Daniels
entities.description: English watchmaker (1926–2011), inventor of the co-axial escapement and mentor of Roger W. Smith.

entities.name: Ludwig Oechslin
entities.description: Horologist-scholar behind Ulysse Nardin's astronomical Trilogy of Time and the Freak.

entities.name: Max Bill
entities.description: Bauhaus-trained designer whose 1960s Junghans clocks and watches remain in production.

entities.name: Roger Tallon
entities.description: French industrial designer (TGV) who created Lip's Mach 2000 collection in 1973.

entities.name: Hans Hilfiker
entities.description: SBB engineer who designed the 1944 Swiss railway clock, licensed to Mondaine since 1986.

entities.name: Jacques Helleu
entities.description: Chanel artistic director who designed the J12.

entities.name: Walter Lange
entities.description: Great-grandson of Ferdinand Adolph Lange who re-founded A. Lange & Söhne in 1990 with Günter Blümlein.

entities.name: Guillaume Laidet
entities.description: French entrepreneur who relaunched Nivada Grenchen (2018) and Vulcain (2021).

entities.name: Tom Kartsotis
entities.description: Co-founder of Fossil (1984) and founder of Shinola (2011) via Bedrock Manufacturing.

entities.name: Webb C. Ball
entities.description: Cleveland jeweller who set US railroad timekeeping standards after the 1891 Kipton wreck and founded Ball Watch Co.

entities.name: Vianney Halter
entities.description: Independent watchmaker, THA co-founder, creator of Harry Winston Opus 3 and Louis Erard collaborator.

entities.name: Max Hetzel
entities.description: Engineer who invented the tuning-fork Accutron movement for Bulova (1960).
